title: C2: logit_calib.cpp — Deville-Sarndal logit Newton solver (bounds by construction)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Implement logit_calibrate(CalibState& st) in src/logit_calib.cpp: cells_per_cat, cat_offset, Newton loop (w/D_eff from logit link, residuals b, N via compute_normal_equations, LDLT solve), degenerate cell handling, check_convergence, weight reconstruction.
* **Why:** This is the core Part 2 solver. T5-T8 turn GREEN when this lands with the bridge. Bounds enforced by construction via logit link — no std::clamp needed on weights.
* **Reference Data:** Spec Part 2 algorithm section. Functions from calib_linalg.hpp: compute_normal_equations(ct, D_eff, N, cat_offset, K, nct), ldlt_factor_inplace(N, nct, 1e-10), ldlt_solve(N, nct, b). D_eff[c]=(U-L)×σ(z)×(1-σ(z)) from Deville-Sarndal 1992 eq 8. Functions from calib_dispatch.hpp: compute_cell_metrics + check_convergence.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/calib_linalg.hpp (normal equations functions), src/calib_dispatch.hpp, src/greg.cpp (template Newton pattern), src/logit_calib.hpp.
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | cat_offset[k] = sum of cat_counts[0..k-1]; nct = total categories |
| **Logic** | z_c = sum_k lambda[cat_offset[k] + g_per_cell[k][c]]; clamp z to [-700, 700] to prevent exp overflow |
| **Logic** | w[c] = L_cell[c] + (U_cell[c]-L_cell[c]) * sigma(z_c) — bounds enforced analytically |
| **Logic** | D_eff[c] = (U_cell[c]-L_cell[c]) * sigma * (1-sigma) — Hessian for Newton weight |
| **Logic** | On compute_normal_equations failure → RK_ERR_INFEAS with 'logit: singular normal equations (degenerate bounds)' |
| **Logic** | On ldlt_factor_inplace failure → RK_ERR_INFEAS with diagnostic |
| **Logic** | Convergence: compute_cell_metrics(st, ct, w, W_total, bucket_scratch) + check_convergence() — NOT hand-rolled pct_tol check |
| **Logic** | Post-loop: RK_ERR_BUDGET if best_resid < initial_resid*0.999, else RK_ERR_STALL. Never RK_ERR_NOCONV |
| **Logic** | Weight reconstruction: w[i] = st.weights[i] * w_best[cell_of[i]] / X_init[cell_of[i]] |
| **Logic** | kMaxNewtonIters = 50 (hard cap, user's max_iterations honors this) |
| **Boundary** | Never set std::clamp on w[c] — logit link guarantees bounds |
| **Boundary** | n=0 guard: if (st.n <= 0) return RK_ERR_BADARG |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/greg.cpp for Newton + LDLT pattern; read src/calib_linalg.hpp for function signatures.
2. Implement logit_calibrate:
   (a) cells_per_cat construction (same as Greenkhorn/raking pattern)
   (b) cat_offset[K] and nct computation
   (c) X_init[c] from design weights; L_cell/U_cell; lambda[nct]=0; w[M_cell]; D_eff[M_cell]; N[nct×nct]; b[nct]
   (d) initial_resid tracking for post-loop classification
   (e) Newton loop:
       - z_c = sum_k lambda[cat_offset[k]+g_per_cell[k][c]], clamped ±700
       - sigma = 1/(1+exp(-z)); w[c] = L+(U-L)*sigma; D_eff[c]=(U-L)*sigma*(1-sigma)
       - Residuals: b[cat_offset[k]+j] = tau[k][j]*n - sum_{c in bucket(k,j)} w[c]
       - compute_normal_equations; ldlt_factor_inplace; ldlt_solve → b=Δλ
       - lambda += b
       - compute_cell_metrics + check_convergence; best-iterate tracking
   (f) Post-loop status
   (g) Weight reconstruction from w_best
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — must compile clean.
4. devtools::test() — FAIL unchanged.
5. git add src/logit_calib.cpp && git commit -m 'feat(logit): implement logit_calibrate — Deville-Sarndal 1992 Newton solver, bounds by construction'

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id":"C2","success":true,"data":{"compiles":true,"key_invariants":{"z_clamped":true,"no_weight_clamp":true,"check_convergence_used":true,"budget_stall_status":true}},"error_log":null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] src/logit_calib.cpp implements logit_calibrate
- [ ] z clamped to ±700; no std::clamp on w[c]
- [ ] compute_cell_metrics + check_convergence (not hand-rolled pct_tol)
- [ ] RK_ERR_INFEAS on singular N or LDLT failure with informative message
- [ ] Never RK_ERR_NOCONV=1 returned
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . clean
- [ ] Committed

title: B2: greenkhorn.cpp — full Greenkhorn solver (argmax IPF + incremental bucket sums)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Implement greenkhorn_solve(CalibState& st) in src/greenkhorn.cpp: cells_per_cat construction, W-incremental maintenance, argmax errRp selection, single-margin IPF update, incremental bucket-sum updates, best-iterate tracking, check_convergence, weight reconstruction.
* **Why:** This is the core Part 1 solver. T1-T4 turn GREEN when this lands with the bridge (Epic D).
* **Reference Data:** Spec Part 1 algorithm section. Key functions from calib_dispatch.hpp: compute_cell_metrics(st,ct,X,W,bucket), check_convergence(cfg,m,prev_metric,tol_abs). Pattern from src/raking.cpp lines 82-100 for cells_per_cat construction.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/greenkhorn.hpp (B1), src/calib_dispatch.hpp (check_convergence, compute_cell_metrics), src/cell_table.hpp (CellTable: g_per_cell, cell_of, M_cell, n_per_cell), src/types.hpp (CalibState).
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | cells_per_cat built locally: for c in M_cell: g_per_cell[k][c] → cells_per_cat[k][g].push_back(c) |
| **Logic** | W maintained incrementally: W += delta per cell update (not recomputed from scratch) |
| **Logic** | W<=0 guard before scale factor: if (W<=0.0) { RK_ERR_INFEAS; break; } |
| **Logic** | S_flat[k*S_stride+j] recomputed exactly from cells after each bucket update (clamp may cause drift) |
| **Logic** | check_convergence via compute_cell_metrics every kErrCheckInterval=10 iterations |
| **Logic** | Best-iterate: X_best snapshot when errRp < best_errRp; return X_best not X |
| **Logic** | Status: if loop exhausts iter and still no convergence: BUDGET if improving, STALL if plateau |
| **Logic** | Weight reconstruction: w[i] = st.weights[i] * X_best[cell_of[i]] / X_init[cell_of[i]] |
| **Boundary** | Never call std::clamp with L>U — validate min_weight<=max_weight before solver |
| **Boundary** | errRp recompute for ALL k after each step (O(Σ cat_counts)) |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/raking.cpp for structural pattern; read src/calib_dispatch.hpp for check_convergence/compute_cell_metrics signatures.
2. Implement greenkhorn_solve with:
   (a) cells_per_cat construction (mirrors raking.cpp lines 82-100)
   (b) X[c] init from design weights; X_init[c] saved; L_cell/U_cell per cell
   (c) W = sum(X); S_flat[K×max_cats] init; errRp[K] init
   (d) bucket_scratch[max_cats] for compute_cell_metrics
   (e) Main loop: W<=0 guard → k*=argmax → per-j update (f=W×τ/S, per-c clamp+delta+W+S updates) → S[k*][j] recompute → errRp update → best-iterate → convergence check
   (f) Post-loop: BUDGET/STALL status via prev_metric comparison
   (g) Weight reconstruction from X_best via cell_of[i]
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -5 — must compile clean.
4. devtools::test() 2>&1 | tail -3 — FAIL unchanged.
5. Manual RED check: harvest(df,tgt,method='greenkhorn') still errors (bridge not wired).
6. git add src/greenkhorn.cpp && git commit -m 'feat(greenkhorn): implement greenkhorn_solve — greedy coordinate-descent IPF with incremental bucket sums'

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id":"B2","success":true,"data":{"compiles":true,"key_invariants":{"W_incremental":true,"W0_guard":true,"X_best_returned":true,"cells_per_cat_local":true}},"error_log":null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] src/greenkhorn.cpp implements greenkhorn_solve
- [ ] cells_per_cat built locally (not from CellTable)
- [ ] W maintained incrementally; W<=0 guard present
- [ ] S[k*][j] recomputed exactly after each bucket update
- [ ] check_convergence + compute_cell_metrics used (no hand-rolled pct_tol check)
- [ ] X_best returned (not X)
- [ ] Status: BUDGET=4 or STALL=5 (never NOCONV=1)
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . clean
- [ ] Committed
notes:
SQUAREM IN SCOPE (user confirmed). When st.accelerate=TRUE:
F_eval = K greedy Greenkhorn steps sorted ONCE at round start (NOT re-sorted per F_eval call).
This makes F_eval stationary → SQUAREM valid. Sort order fixed at round entry:
  std::sort(order, [&](a,b){ return errRp[a] > errRp[b]; });
  for ki in 0..K-1: single_greenkhorn_step(order[ki], X, W, S, errRp)
Then SQUAREM CBB step mirrors raking.cpp lines 351-480:
  sq_X_snap = X; sq_w1 = F_eval(X); sq_w2 = F_eval(sq_w1)
  alpha = -||sq_w1-sq_X_snap||_obs / ||sq_w2-2*sq_w1+sq_X_snap||_obs
  sq_X_star = sq_X_snap - 2*alpha*r + alpha^2*v
  sq_X_star = F_eval(sq_X_star)  [stabilization]
  Accept sq_X_star or fall back to sq_w2 on violation
Key difference from raking: greedy sort allowed (and applied) inside F_eval.
Key constraint: Sort at ENTRY of F_eval, not per individual step within F_eval.

title: B10: sinkhorn.cpp Dykstra a[] must be zeroed when !needs_projection
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Zero a[c] for all cells when the projection step is skipped (!needs_projection) to prevent phantom KL correction accumulation in the Dykstra iteration.
* **Why:** sinkhorn.cpp:150-156: a[c] accumulates log(X[c]) - log(X_proj[c]) only when needs_projection=true. When the box constraint is inactive (needs_projection=false), a[] is left dirty from the previous active iteration. Next time the projection activates, a[] carries phantom mass from the stale correction — drifts the KL iterate away from the Dykstra fixed point.
* **Reference Data:** sinkhorn.cpp lines 148-157 (Dykstra correction block). a[] is a vector of doubles (size M_cell). needs_projection = (bisect_capacity returned meaningful X_proj). When inactive: X_proj = X; X[c] already set; a[] should track zero (no correction applied).

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/sinkhorn.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | In the `if (needs_projection) { ... } else { ... }` block: add in the else branch: `for (int c = 0; c < ct.M_cell; c++) a[c] = 0.0;` |
| **Logic** | OR: zero a[] only when transitioning from active to inactive (track prev_needs_projection) — simpler is the full zero |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT zero a[] inside the if(needs_projection) block — the accumulation there is correct |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read sinkhorn.cpp lines 140-165 to understand the correction accumulation logic.
2. Write a test: problem where the box constraint is transiently inactive for several iterations then becomes active again — verify the KL iterate is correct vs reference.
3. Add a[c]=0.0 zero-out in the else branch.
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
5. devtools::test() — calibration-solvers tests (sinkhorn) must pass.
6. Commit: fix(sinkhorn): zero Dykstra a[] when projection inactive to prevent phantom correction.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "B10", "success": true, "data": {"file": "src/sinkhorn.cpp", "test": "PASS"}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] a[] zeroed when !needs_projection
- [ ] Test: transient-inactive projection → correct KL iterate
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds; devtools::test() no regressions
- [ ] Committed
notes: GATE FINDING: Original fix (zeroing a[] when !needs_projection) was WRONG. a[] is a cross-iteration accumulated Dykstra correction that must NOT be zeroed on non-binding projections — zeroing would destroy accumulated history. The existing else-branch no-op is correct standard Dykstra. Plan changed to comment-only fix: add comment explaining why a[] must not be zeroed in the else branch.

title: B17: Guard PLATEAU rule in calib_dispatch against prev=0 false convergence
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add prev > 0 guard to the PLATEAU convergence rule in calib_dispatch.hpp so prev=0 initialization never fires false convergence on iter 1.
* **Why:** calib_dispatch.hpp:93: `if (std::isfinite(prev)) { converged = !(curr < prev*(1.0-tol)); }`. With prev=0.0 (wrong initialization by a caller): curr >= 0 = prev*(1-tol) always → converged=true on iteration 1. Any caller that leaves prev=0.0 (instead of +inf as the doc comments require) gets false convergence. The guard is one line; the doc contract alone is insufficient protection.
* **Reference Data:** calib_dispatch.hpp line 93. apply_rule function. prev must be initialized to std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity() before first call. CalibRule::PLATEAU is rule=2.

title: B12: compute_margin_errRp must return +inf (not 0) when W_total<=0
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Change ieppa.cpp compute_margin_errRp_linear and compute_margin_errRp_log to return std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity() instead of 0.0 when W_total <= 0.
* **Why:** ieppa.cpp:589,605: `if (W_total <= 0.0) return 0.0;`. Returning 0.0 makes the error metric appear 'perfect'. The greedy scheduler then picks k_star=0 with best=0.0 and applies margins to a degenerate-state solver, producing meaningless updates. The correct sentinel for 'cannot compute error' is +inf — this will never trigger false convergence and will cause the greedy to correctly avoid this margin.
* **Reference Data:** ieppa.cpp lines 589,605 (both linear and log path versions of compute_margin_errRp). W_total is the sum of all X[c] in the margin's cells. W_total <= 0 means the solver state is degenerate.

| **Logic** | Verify: greedy scheduler compares errRp; +inf will never be selected as best (it's > any finite value) — check greedy min-selection logic |
| **Boundary** | Both linear and log path functions must be fixed |

title: B9: Wire raking is_infeasible flag to RK_ERR_INFEAS on post-loop stall path
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Remove the dead is_infeasible variable from raking.cpp OR wire it to set res.status=RK_ERR_INFEAS on the post-loop stall exit path.
* **Why:** raking.cpp sets is_infeasible=true inside water_fill_cat (lines 183, 197, 287) but NEVER reads it. RK_ERR_INFEAS is never returned from the raking solver regardless of structural infeasibility in the bounded raking. The comment at line 593-595 says 'do NOT override with INFEAS here' but there is no INFEAS override ANYWHERE in raking — the flag is purely dead code.
* **Reference Data:** raking.cpp: is_infeasible set at lines 183, 197, 287. is_infeasible never read. Post-loop exit paths at lines 591-619. RK_ERR_INFEAS=2 in leafblower.h. water_fill_cat: infeasible when sum(L_c for cells in bucket j) > target_mass for bucket j.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/raking.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | After the main while-loop, if is_infeasible is true AND res.status == RK_ERR_STALL: override to RK_ERR_INFEAS |
| **Logic** | Only override on STALL (not BUDGET) — INFEAS means no feasible solution; BUDGET means ran out of time but feasibility unknown |

title: B2: lbfgsb_solver must emit RK_ERR_BUDGET(4) and RK_ERR_STALL(5) on exit
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Differentiate lbfgsb_solver exit paths: return RK_ERR_BUDGET(4) when iteration budget exhausted with gn >= tol; return RK_ERR_STALL(5) when gradient stalls without convergence.
* **Why:** lbfgsb_solver.cpp:305 sets status unconditionally as: `res.status = converged ? RK_OK : RK_ERR_NOCONV;`. NOCONV(1) is a legacy alias — no solver should emit it. harvest.R has dead code at s==4 and s==5 for lbfgsb because it never gets there. Users get no information about WHY lbfgsb failed.
* **Reference Data:** lbfgsb_solver.cpp line 305. RK_ERR_BUDGET=4 means 'still improving, increase max_iter'. RK_ERR_STALL=5 means 'at constrained optimum, weights are valid'. Loop at lines 602-659. Convergence check at lines 291-303: converged = curr_metric < cfg.pct_tol. BUDGET: iter==max_iter AND gn >= tol. STALL: successive gn changes < eps (gradient plateau).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/lbfgsb_solver.cpp, src/leafblower.h (status code definitions)
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Track prev_gn across iterations; if abs(gn - prev_gn)/max(prev_gn,1e-15) < stall_eps (e.g. 1e-6) for N consecutive iters (e.g. 5), set status=STALL |
| **Logic** | If loop exits via iter==max_iter and !converged: status=BUDGET |
| **Logic** | RK_OK only when convergence check fires |
| **Logic** | STALL should only fire AFTER at least burnin=10 iterations |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT emit NOCONV(1) from lbfgsb — it is a legacy alias |
| **Boundary** | harvest.R already maps s==4L to 'budget' warning and s==5L to 'stall_kl' message; no harvest.R changes needed |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read lbfgsb_solver.cpp fully — find the loop structure, gn computation, exit conditions.
2. Write tests: (a) max_iter=5 on a problem that needs 100 iters → expect status==4L (BUDGET); (b) problem at exact constrained optimum with tiny gradient → expect status==5L (STALL) or 0L (OK).
3. Add prev_gn tracking and stall counter inside the L-BFGS-B loop.
4. Update the status assignment at line 305 to use the three-way logic.
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
6. Run tests — confirm BUDGET and STALL codes emitted correctly.
7. devtools::test() — no regressions.
8. Commit: fix(lbfgsb): emit RK_ERR_BUDGET(4)/RK_ERR_STALL(5) instead of legacy NOCONV.

title: B6: Validate metric/rule names in harvest.R before .Call to prevent NULL→UB in C bridge
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add explicit validation of metric/rule/stop_when names in harvest.R's parse_convergence() before the .Call, so unknown names produce a clear R error instead of NULL→integer(0)→C UB.

title: B4: Wrap solver calls in try/catch to prevent PROTECT stack corruption
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Wrap all lbw::*_solve() dispatch calls in r_bridge.cpp in try/catch so C++ exceptions never escape past PROTECT'd SEXPs.
* **Why:** C++ exceptions do not unwind R's protection stack (PROTECT/UNPROTECT). Any std::bad_alloc or other exception thrown inside a solver will corrupt the R protection stack, causing GC errors or crashes in subsequent allocations. R's own Rf_error() uses longjmp and is safe; C++ exceptions are not.
* **Reference Data:** r_bridge.cpp lines 533-618. The PROTECT count at solver entry is ~0 (SEXPs allocated post-solve) but PROTECT calls inside the dispatch block (e.g., bw_sxp at line 591) are at risk.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/r_bridge.cpp source file.
* **Format:** C++ source — read the full dispatch block from line ~366 to ~520.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Wrap the entire lbw::*_solve() call (and its result extraction) in try { ... } catch (const std::exception& e) { UNPROTECT(N); Rf_error("leafblower: solver error: %s", e.what()); } |
| **Logic** | N in UNPROTECT must be the exact count of PROTECT calls before the try block |
| **Format** | No bare catch(...) — catch std::exception only |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT wrap Rf_error, Rf_warning (they longjmp and must not be inside try) |
| **Tone** | Compile gate: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . must succeed after change |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read r_bridge.cpp in full; count PROTECT calls before each solver dispatch.
2. Write a test that calls the solver with an input designed to trigger allocation failure (not always possible; at minimum write a test confirming no regression).
3. Wrap the solver dispatch block in try { auto result = dispatch(...); } catch (const std::exception& e) { UNPROTECT(count); Rf_error("...", e.what()); }.
4. Verify PROTECT count N matches the wrapping.
5. Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . in /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower.
6. Run: Rscript -e "devtools::test()" -- must have same pass/fail count as before.
7. Commit: fix(r_bridge): wrap solver dispatch in try/catch to protect R GC stack.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "B4",
  "success": true,
  "data": { "file": "src/r_bridge.cpp", "protect_count": "N", "test_result": "PASS" },
  "error_log": null
}
```

title: HUMAN: homotopy hypothesis falsified on stepstone-fulldata — choose new approach
description:
WU-6 merge gate FAILS — CONFIRMED with corrected max_err_of() (commit 8c5836f).

Prior max_err_of() had positional-subtraction bug inflating all errors to 0.163+.
Fix: name-aligned subtraction (tab[names(target[[k]])] - target[[k]]).
After fix, autumn correctly shows 1.60e-3 (reference). All leafblower configs
still fail. Bug was NOT masking success.

CORRECTED results (stepstone-fulldata, 1.58M rows, 3000 iters, max_weight=5):
- autumn (reference): max_err = 1.60e-3
- Baseline (overlays off): max_err = 2.223e-3 (39% worse than autumn)
- Greedy only: 3.727e-3 (WORSE than baseline)
- Homotopy+greedy (AB): 6.567e-3 (MUCH worse than baseline)
- All overlay configs degrade vs round-robin baseline

Root cause (confirmed from WU-2.5): stepstone-fulldata is an OSCILLATORY/DIVERGENT
regime (errRp increases from iter ~100 onward). Homotopy+Greenkhorn theory targets
SLOW-RATE convergence. These overlays do not address oscillatory divergence.

Decision needed: (A) stronger global damping (reduce alpha) to suppress oscillation;
(B) reframe target (accept 2.223e-3 = 39% worse than autumn as deliverable);
(C) different algorithmic approach for this regime; (D) abandon P-A/P-B for this dataset.

Code remains on branch feat/ieppa-homotopy-greenkhorn, all WU-1..7 infrastructure intact,

title: fix(greenkhorn): force round-robin sweep when accelerate=TRUE
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Disable greenkhorn's internal per-step argmax selection when accelerate=TRUE, replacing with round-robin so SRAA's fixed-point map is stationary.
* **Why:** Greenkhorn IS the greedy coordinate-descent Sinkhorn: each step picks argmax-violation margin. This non-stationarity (F(X) depends on X's residuals, not just X) breaks SRAA's convergence theory. Benchmark shows greenkhorn+sraa DEFF=2.031 > plain 1.963, wmed=0.439 vs 0.581, wt_kl<0 — SRAA steering to a different, worse attractor.
* **Reference:** Same issue as ieppa's greedy downgrade (B5: 'use_greedy_sraa=false when accelerate=TRUE'). src/greenkhorn.cpp needs the same fix.
* **Note:** In greenkhorn the greedy IS the algorithm (not a scheduler option). With accelerate=TRUE, the full-round-robin sweep inside f_eval_lf already calls apply_single_margin_log/linear for all K margins. Greenkhorn's own F_eval should use round-robin too.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/greenkhorn.cpp — the greenkhorn_solve function
* **Format:** C++17

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | When st.accelerate=TRUE: run all K margins in round-robin order (not argmax). When st.accelerate=FALSE: keep existing greedy argmax behavior. |
| **Format** | Single conditional at solve entry, no duplicate logic |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/greenkhorn.cpp to find the per-step argmax selection loop
2. Add: if (st.accelerate) { log message; use round-robin } else { existing greedy }
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . && Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
4. Verify greenkhorn+sraa benchmark shows DEFF closer to plain greenkhorn

## V. Output Schema
```json
{"task_id": "LBW-XXX", "success": true, "data": {"greenkhorn_sraa_deff_improved": true}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] greenkhorn+sraa uses round-robin when accelerate=TRUE
- [ ] log message '[greenkhorn] greedy disabled under SRAA-m; using round_robin' at verbose>=1
- [ ] all tests pass
- [ ] benchmark shows greenkhorn+sraa DEFF ≈ plain greenkhorn (1.963±0.05)
close_reason: Wrong analysis: greenkhorn's greedy F(X) IS deterministic (same X→same errRp→same argmax). SRAA is valid. No code change needed. wt_kl<0 is a different-attractor issue, not a theory violation.

title: B3: SRAA outer loop with lf_best tracking (replaces for-loop)
description:
## Objective
Replace iter_in_lvl for-loop with SRAA while-loop when accelerate=TRUE && use_linear. Manage lf_best for stall revert, W_best for output, SRAAState lifecycle.

## Input & Guards
- File: src/ieppa.cpp (homotopy level, after linear phase init)
- Guards: Must compile; if/else branch (not alongside old for-loop); F_cur seeded once before loop

## Logic
1. if (st.accelerate && use_linear): SRAA path
2. Init: SRAAState, lf_flat, lf_best, pack lf → lf_flat, seed F_cur
3. while-loop: f_evals_used < budget_lvl && !converged
   - sraa_step(f_eval_lf, lf_flat, {}, {}, ieppa_sraa, apply_clamp=false)
   - Update res.base.iterations = f_evals_used
   - Track best: save W_best (X/X_init) + lf_best if err < best_metric_seen
   - Outer stall guard: if err > best*(1+kSRAAOuterSlack), revert lf_best + reseed F_cur
   - Check convergence
4. else: existing for-loop unchanged

- [ ] lf_best used only for SRAA revert, not for output

title: B1: pack_lf/unpack_lf helpers in ieppa.cpp
description:
## Objective
Implement pack_lf() and unpack_lf() helpers in ieppa.cpp to convert between lf-space (log-factor iterate) and cell-space (X_cur, etc.).

## Input & Guards
- File: src/ieppa.cpp
- Guards: Must compile; no changes to existing non-SRAA code paths; preserve alpha damping in sweep

## Logic
1. pack_lf(lf, dst): O(n_cats_total_with_na) copy lf → dst for SRAA state seeding
2. unpack_lf(src, lf, f_lin, cell_lf, X_cur, ct, X_init, st.K, cat_offset):
   - Copy src → lf
   - Derive f_lin[i] = exp(lf[i]) for all i
   - Rebuild cell_lf[c] = Σ_k lf[cat_offset[k] + g_per_cell[k][c]]
   - X_cur[c] = X_init[c] * exp(cell_lf[c])

## DoD

- [ ] No change to non-SRAA paths (verify with diff)

description:
# T5: Mehrotra + Jacobi
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION (after T4)

## I. Objective
Replace the existing single-step barrier loop in chebyshev_ipm with Mehrotra predictor-corrector + Jacobi diagonal preconditioning. T_cheby_warm and T_cheby_K9 must go GREEN.

## II. Input
src/chebyshev.cpp — the main IPM iteration loop (find via grep kMaxIpm or schur_nu)
Spec §Change 3+4: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-chebyshev-greg-fix.md

## III. Guards
CRITICAL INVARIANTS:
- m > 0 guard: if (m == 0) { mu *= 0.1; continue; }
- N rebuilt fresh EACH iteration (A·D·A^T) — never cached between iterations
- Jacobi scaling applied ONCE before LDLT factorization
- Phase A: LDLT-factor scaled N; solve Phase A RHS (pre-scaled, post-unscale)
- Phase B: REUSE same LDLT (no refactor); solve Phase B RHS (pre-scaled, post-unscale)
- σ = clamp((μ_aff/μ)³, 1e-8, 1.0)
- μ_aff = clamp(dot(x+α*Δx, s+α*Δs)/(2m), 0, μ*100)
- 0.99 damping on step lengths
- Tikhonov fallback if LDLT fails
FORBIDDEN: changing kMaxIpm or existing convergence check; touching r_bridge.cpp/harvest.R

## IV. Logic
1. Read the existing IPM iteration loop in chebyshev.cpp (grep kMaxIpm, schur_nu)
2. Extract the complementarity vectors (x, s) and normal equations build (N = A·D·A^T)
3. Before the loop: understand the existing Schur complement formulation
4. Replace single-step loop body with:
   a. m>0 guard
   b. Rebuild N = A·D·A^T fresh
   c. Jacobi preconditioning: D_jac[j]=1/sqrt(max(N[j*nct+j],1e-12)); scale N in-place
   d. LDLT-factor scaled N once
   e. Phase A: scale rhs_A, solve, unscale Δλ_A
   f. Compute α_aff, μ_aff (with clamp), σ (with clamp)
   g. Phase B: rhs_B = rhs_A + σ*μ - Δx_aff·Δs_aff; scale rhs_B, solve SAME LDLT, unscale Δλ_B
   h. Line search α_p, α_d with 0.99 damping
   i. Update x, λ, s; recompute μ = dot(x,s)/(2m)
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3 → '* DONE (leafblower)'
6. Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter="chebyshev")' → T_cheby_warm GREEN
7. devtools::test() FAIL=3
8. Commit: 'feat(chebyshev): Mehrotra predictor-corrector + Jacobi preconditioning'

## V. Schema
{"task_id":"T5","success":true,"data":{"T_cheby_warm":"PASS","fail_count":3},"error_log":null}

## VI. DoD
- [ ] Mehrotra loop replaces existing single-step loop
- [ ] Jacobi preconditioning on Phase A and Phase B
- [ ] m>0 guard present; σ/μ_aff clamped
- [ ] Phase B reuses Phase A LDLT (confirmed by n_factorizations==iterations)
- [ ] T_cheby_warm GREEN (status=0, finite, ≤ raking)
- [ ] T_cheby_K9 GREEN or SKIP (parquet-dependent)
- [ ] devtools::test() FAIL=3
- [ ] Committed
close_reason: Mehrotra+Jacobi implemented. T_cheby_warm PASS (4.12e-14 < 1e-3). FAIL=3. n_factorizations increments once. Phase B reuses Phase A LDLT.

title: T3: Armijo line search with step-norm guard and pre-allocated buffers
description:
# T3: Armijo Line Search for logit_calib.cpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add Armijo backtracking line search to logit_calibrate() Newton loop: pre-allocate trial buffers, cap step via max_delta_z norm guard, backtrack until sufficient decrease, log warning if all halvings exhausted.
* **Why:** Without line search, Newton steps can be arbitrarily large, saturating cells even from a good initialization. Armijo guarantees progress toward the calibration fixed point.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §Layer 1 + Security Fix 1 (norm guard) + Security Fix 2 (pre-alloc) + Designer Fix 1 (stall warning). See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-sv89-logit-newton-fix.md.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp after T1+T2 applied. Target: the Newton for-loop.
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | kMaxHalvings=10, kArmijoC=0.01, kMaxDeltaZ=2.0 — constexpr at function top |
| **Logic** | ORDERING: norm guard runs AFTER ldlt_solve (when b = delta_lambda, not residuals) |
| **Logic** | Pre-alloc: w_trial(M_cell), b_trial(nct), lambda_trial(nct) declared BEFORE Newton loop |
| **Logic** | Armijo condition: resid_sq_trial < resid_sq_0 * (1.0 - kArmijoC * alpha) |
| **Logic** | If all halvings exhausted with no improvement: accept alpha anyway (last alpha); emit st.log() warning if verbose>=1 |
| **Logic** | Recompute w_trial from lambda_trial (logit link); recompute b_trial residuals |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change Newton loop iteration count (kMaxNewtonIters=50) |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change check_convergence call — it remains at end of each iteration |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/logit_calib.cpp — understand current Newton loop structure.
2. Add constexpr: kMaxHalvings=10, kArmijoC=0.01, kMaxDeltaZ=2.0
3. BEFORE Newton loop: declare w_trial(ct.M_cell, 0.0), b_trial(nct, 0.0), lambda_trial(nct, 0.0)
4. INSIDE Newton loop, AFTER ldlt_solve (b = delta_lambda):
   a. Norm guard: compute max_delta_z over all cells (sum |b[cat_offset[k]+g]| per cell); alpha_max = min(1.0, kMaxDeltaZ / max_delta_z) if max_delta_z>0
   b. double alpha = alpha_max; resid_sq_0 = sum(b_current^2) [b_current = current residuals, NOT delta_lambda]
   c. Armijo loop: for halv in 0..kMaxHalvings: fill lambda_trial, recompute w_trial from logit link, compute b_trial; if resid_sq_trial < resid_sq_0*(1-kArmijoC*alpha): break; alpha *= 0.5
   d. If !armijo_improved && verbose>=1: st.log('[logit] Armijo exhausted (alpha=%.2e)', alpha)
   e. lambda += alpha * b [where b = delta_lambda from ldlt_solve]
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3 → '* DONE'
6. Rscript -e 'devtools::test()' 2>&1 | tail -3 → FAIL == 3
7. Quick test: run harvest on 2-margin K=2 problem → must converge
8. git commit: 'fix(logit): Armijo line search with step-norm guard prevents Newton divergence'

- [ ] Armijo condition checks calibration residuals (not step size)

title: T2: Design-weight initialization — place lambda in convergence basin
description:
# T2: Design-weight initialization for logit_calib.cpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the lambda=0 cold-start in logit_calibrate() with lambda_0 computed from a LS solve that places the starting point where sigma(z_c) ≈ normalized design weight — preventing the cold-start saturation cascade.
* **Why:** lambda=0 gives w[c]=2.5*n_per_cell (midpoint), far from calibrated solution. First Newton step overshoots. Design-weight initialization places lambda_0 such that the starting weights approximate the design weights, keeping sigma away from 0 and 1 on the first iteration.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §Layer 2 — Design-Weight Initialization. Uses calib_linalg.hpp: compute_normal_equations(ct, D_ones, N, cat_offset, K, nct), ldlt_factor_inplace(N, nct, 1e-10), ldlt_solve(N, nct, b). All already included.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp — find where lambda is initialized (currently near line 79: std::vector<double> lambda(nct, 0.0)).
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | kInitSigmaEps = 1e-4 — clips sigma_target to [1e-4, 1-1e-4] to bound z_target |
| **Logic** | Degenerate: if (U_cell[c] <= L_cell[c] + 1e-12) set z_target[c] = 0.0 |
| **Logic** | Clip X_init outside [L, U]: sigma_target = clamp((X_init-L)/(U-L), 1e-4, 1-1e-4) |
| **Logic** | AA^T initialization uses compute_normal_equations with D_eff=1 (all-ones D vector) |
| **Logic** | lambda = ldlt result (b_init after solve), NOT accumulated with 0-init lambda |
| **Format** | Insert initialization block BEFORE the Newton for-loop, AFTER lambda is declared |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change the Newton loop itself in this task (that is T3) |
| **Boundary** | scratch vectors: z_target(M_cell), D_ones(M_cell, 1.0), b_init(nct, 0.0), N_init(nct*nct, 0.0) |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/logit_calib.cpp — find lambda declaration (~line 79) and Newton loop start.
2. Add constexpr: `constexpr double kInitSigmaEps = 1e-4;`
3. After lambda declaration, insert initialization block:
   a. Allocate z_target(M_cell), D_ones(M_cell, 1.0), b_init(nct, 0.0), N_init(nct*nct, 0.0)
   b. For each cell c: compute sigma_target, z_target[c] = logit(sigma_target)
   c. For each (k,j) bucket: b_init[cat_offset[k]+j] = sum of z_target[c] over bucket
   d. compute_normal_equations(ct, D_ones.data(), N_init.data(), cat_offset.data(), K, (size_t)nct)
   e. ldlt_factor_inplace(N_init.data(), (size_t)nct, 1e-10) — check return value; if not RK_OK, leave lambda=0 (fall back silently)
   f. ldlt_solve(N_init.data(), (size_t)nct, b_init.data()) — b_init is now lambda_0
   g. lambda = b_init (assign, not accumulate)
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3 → '* DONE'
5. devtools::test() 2>&1 | tail -3 → FAIL == 3
6. Quick sanity: verify that running harvest(df,tgt,method='logit') still works and gives finite weights
7. git commit: 'fix(logit): initialize lambda from design-weight logit-inverse to prevent cold-start saturation'

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "T2", "success": true, "data": {"file": "src/logit_calib.cpp", "change": "design-weight init block inserted"}, "error_log": null}
```

# Epic: sv89 — Logit Newton Stabilization

## Goal
Fix logit_calibrate() divergence on large-K problems via three surgical changes to src/logit_calib.cpp: D_eff floor, design-weight initialization, and Armijo line search with step-norm guard.

title: bug: logit diverges on large-K problems (lambda=0 warmstart + Newton overshoot)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Fix logit_calibrate to converge on the stepstone benchmark (K=9, n=1.58M, max_weight=5). Currently: max_err=1.0, DEFF=527k, ESS=3 — completely diverged.
* **Why:** lambda=0 warmstart → sigma(0)=0.5 → w[c]=2.5×n_per_cell. First Newton step on K=9 conflicting margins produces large Δλ, pushing some lambda to extreme values → sigma→0 or 1 → D_eff[c]=(U-L)×sigma×(1-sigma)≈0 for those cells → column of N is near-zero → LDLT solve produces unbounded Δλ → next step worse → divergence spiral. Stepstone has large sparse cell tables where this degeneracy is likely.
* **Evidence:** Benchmark: logit status=0 (reports converged!), iters=9 Newton steps, max_err=1.0, DEFF=527,577, ESS=3. Pearson r with ieppa = 0.006 (near-zero correlation — essentially random weights).
* **Root cause hypotheses:**
  1. No Newton step damping — Δλ can be unbounded
  2. lambda=0 gives poor warmstart for large-K problems (sigma=0.5 is far from solution)
  3. check_convergence fires on a false convergence metric before weights are meaningful
  4. kEps=1e-10 Tikhonov regularization insufficient for near-zero D_eff cells
* **Fix options (evaluate in order):**
  A. Add line search / damping: alpha = argmin ||b(lambda + alpha*delta_lambda)|| (bisection, max 5 halvings). Simplest fix.
  B. Increase Tikhonov regularization for near-degenerate D_eff: if min(D_eff) < threshold, increase kEps.
  C. Warmstart from raking solution: run a few raking steps to get a better lambda_0 before Newton.
  D. Cap |Δλ[j]| per step to prevent runaway updates.
* **Recommended:** Option A (damped Newton / line search). Standard practice for logit calibration (survey::calib with method='logit' uses step-halving by default).

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp — Newton loop lines ~50-120.
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Damped Newton: after computing delta_lambda, find alpha in (0,1] via bisection on ||b||; accept step if ||b(lambda+alpha*Δλ)|| < ||b(lambda)|| * (1-0.01*alpha) (Armijo condition) |
| **Logic** | Max halvings = 10; if no improvement found, take smallest step (alpha=2^-10) |
| **Logic** | Recompute w[c], D_eff[c] at trial lambda before evaluating Armijo |
| **Boundary** | Damping adds O(M_cell × halvings) cost per Newton step — acceptable |
| **Boundary** | T5-T8 tests must still pass after fix |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. After ldlt_solve gives delta_lambda in b[], add Armijo line search:
   - alpha = 1.0; halving_count = 0
   - while halving_count < kMaxHalvings:
     - trial_lambda = lambda + alpha * delta_lambda
     - recompute w_trial[c] from trial_lambda
     - recompute residuals b_trial[]
     - if ||b_trial|| < ||b_current|| * (1 - 0.01*alpha): break
     - alpha *= 0.5; halving_count++
   - lambda += alpha * delta_lambda
2. Run stepstone benchmark: logit should converge within 50 Newton steps.
3. Verify T5-T8 still pass.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "logit_damping", "success": true, "data": {"stepstone_max_err": "<0.01", "t5_t8_pass": true}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Stepstone logit: max_err < 0.01 (comparable to raking 1.60e-3)
- [ ] Stepstone logit: DEFF in reasonable range (1.5-2.5)
- [ ] T5-T8 tests GREEN
- [ ] devtools::test() FAIL unchanged

description:

| **Logic** | Root cause hypothesis 1: u[c] resets at lines 692+708 (overflow fallback) kill accumulated dual → ADMM degenerates to hard clamp on any problem that hits overflow even once |
| **Logic** | Root cause hypothesis 2: On tight-bounds problems, the fixed point of ADMM z-update coincides with the hard-clamp fixed point (same attractor basin) |
| **Logic** | Root cause hypothesis 3: The convergence check triggers before u[c] has accumulated meaningful signal (50 iters default) |
| **Boundary** | Fix must make T3 pass: me_soft < me_hard on set.seed(3), n=5000, max_weight=1.8, 5-category problem |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

User explicitly wanted ALM (Augmented Lagrangian Method) to REPLACE the hard cap. ALM: dual variable per cell accumulates violation; penalty term in BCD objective drives X toward feasible set without clamping. title: R7: chebyshev negative slack must warn and promote to INFEAS
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In chebyshev.cpp, when s_up[m] or s_dn[m] would be negative (before std::max(..., kEps) clamping), log a warning and promote status to RK_ERR_INFEAS.
* **Why:** chebyshev.cpp:443-449: `s_up[m] = std::max(T_flat[m]*W_upd + w_kj[m]*delta - S[m], kEps);`. When the bracket is negative, the slack is set to kEps silently — the LP interior invariant s*y ≈ mu is broken for those margins. This is a latent convergence stall source. The correct action is to flag potential infeasibility.
* **Reference Data:** chebyshev.cpp lines 443-449. kEps is a small positive constant. Negative slack means T_flat[m]*W + w_kj[m]*delta < S[m] — infeasibility indicator.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/chebyshev.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Before the std::max clamp: if (T_flat[m]*W_upd + w_kj[m]*delta - S[m] < 0) { st.log("[chebyshev] slack violation at margin m"); res.status = RK_ERR_INFEAS; } |
| **Logic** | Only promote to INFEAS if this occurs more than kInfeasPersistence consecutive iterations (to avoid transient false positives) |
| **Logic** | Still apply the std::max clamp after the check (don't change clamp behavior) |
| **Boundary** | Log warning at verbose >= 1; INFEAS only after persistent violation |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read chebyshev.cpp lines 440-455 — identify all slack update sites.
2. Add a slack_violations counter; increment when any s_up/s_dn would be negative.
3. If counter > kInfeasPersistence: res.status = RK_ERR_INFEAS; break.
4. Reset counter when no violations.
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
6. devtools::test() — no regressions on non-infeasible inputs.
7. Commit: fix(chebyshev): flag INFEAS on persistent negative slack; log warning.

title: R1: Cache greg.cpp Newton factorization; only recompute on active-set change
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Cache the LDLT factorization of N = A*diag(X_init)*A^T in greg.cpp; only recompute it when the active set (fixed_lo[], fixed_hi[]) changes between Newton iterations.
* **Why:** greg.cpp computes N and its LDLT factorization from scratch at every Newton step. N = A*diag(X_init)*A^T where X_init is CONSTANT — the normal equations do not change unless the active set changes. For kMaxNewtonIters=10 steps with unchanged active set, the factorization is recomputed 10× identically. Each factorization is O(nct^3) where nct = total categories.
* **Reference Data:** greg.cpp lines ~75-95 (compute_normal_equations call + ldlt_factor_inplace). fixed_lo[], fixed_hi[] arrays track which cells are at bounds. active set changes when any cell transitions to/from bounds.

## II. Input Specification

* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Track active set hash (or compare fixed_lo/fixed_hi between iterations). If unchanged: skip recomputation; reuse cached L matrix. |
| **Logic** | On first iteration: always compute. |
| **Logic** | When any cell transitions: invalidate cache and recompute |
| **Format** | Use a bool active_set_changed flag: compare old vs new fixed_lo/fixed_hi arrays |
| **Boundary** | N is nct x nct where nct = Σ cat_counts[k] — typically 10-100 |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read greg.cpp fully — find factorization call site and active-set tracking.
2. Add: std::vector<bool> prev_fixed_lo, prev_fixed_hi; bool need_refactor = true;
3. At start of each Newton iter: compare current fixed_lo/hi with prev; set need_refactor accordingly. Update prev arrays.
4. Only call compute_normal_equations + ldlt_factor_inplace when need_refactor.

title: B15: chebyshev alpha_p/alpha_d floor 1e-10 can violate IPM interior invariant
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the alpha_p = max(alpha_p, 1e-10) floor in chebyshev.cpp with a proper handling that either accepts degeneration or uses a safe fraction-to-boundary formula.
* **Why:** chebyshev.cpp:424: `alpha_p = std::max(alpha_p, 1e-10);` forces forward progress when the Newton direction would drive a slack to zero. When the natural alpha_p is near-zero (degenerate direction), forcing 1e-10 can produce s_lo[c] < 0 or s_up[c] < 0 — violating the interior-point invariant. Non-monotone behaviour results.
* **Reference Data:** chebyshev.cpp line 424 (alpha_p floor). The standard IPM safe step is: alpha = min over i where ds[i]<0: -0.99*s[i]/ds[i]. Forcing 1e-10 violates this. Same issue at alpha_d line.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/chebyshev.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Remove the 1e-10 floor. If alpha_p == 0 (exact degeneracy), accept the zero step and iterate again — OR use the fraction-to-boundary formula with factor 0.995 |
| **Logic** | Option A: alpha_p = max(alpha_p, 0.0) (no floor). If alpha_p==0 → skip step, count as degenerate iter |
| **Logic** | Option B (preferred): use standard 0.995*fraction-to-boundary for alpha_p and alpha_d |
| **Boundary** | Both alpha_p AND alpha_d floors must be fixed |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read chebyshev.cpp line-search section (lines ~418-435 for alpha_p and equivalent for alpha_d).
2. Understand the current fraction-to-boundary computation.
3. Replace floor with proper fraction-to-boundary: alpha_p = min over c: (ds[c]<0 ? -0.995*s[c]/ds[c] : 1.0); then clamp to [0,1].
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
5. devtools::test() — chebyshev tests pass; verify no new convergence failures.
6. Commit: fix(chebyshev): replace alpha floor 1e-10 with proper fraction-to-boundary formula.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "B15", "success": true, "data": {"file": "src/chebyshev.cpp", "formula": "fraction-to-boundary"}, "error_log": null}
```

- [ ] alpha_p and alpha_d use fraction-to-boundary (no 1e-10 floor)
- [ ] Interior invariant s > 0 maintained after step
- [ ] devtools::test() chebyshev tests pass
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds; no regressions

title: R8: Assert greedy scheduler and SQUAREM accelerate are mutually exclusive in raking.cpp
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add a C++ assertion (or forced override) in raking.cpp that disables the greedy scheduler when accelerate=true (SQUAREM mode).
* **Why:** raking.cpp:159 + 354: greedy scheduler and SQUAREM are mutually exclusive but not enforced. Under SQUAREM, F_eval is invoked on different iterates (X, w1, X*); greedy sorts margins by errRp_k before each F call making F non-stationary — SQUAREM requires identical F for F(X) and F(F(X)). If a user sets both accelerate=true and scheduler=GREEDY, behavior is silently wrong. The comment '(void)errRp_w1' acknowledges the problem but doesn't fix it.
* **Reference Data:** raking.cpp lines 159 (use_greedy declaration), 256 (greedy sort inside F_eval), 277 (errRp_k update). CalibState.accelerate field. harvest.R:222 has the guard in R but not in C++.

title: R4: Fix estimate_M_cell to return correct bound for K>8 margins
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the `if (K > 8) return n;` shortcut in estimate_M_cell with min(product_of_cat_counts, n) to avoid misrouting small-cell problems to iEPPA.
* **Why:** estimate_M_cell currently returns n for any K>8, making AUTO route everything to iEPPA regardless of actual cell count. For K=9 with 2 categories each, M_cell <= 512 << n — raking is the correct choice. Wrong routing wastes time on the heavier iEPPA algorithm.
* **Reference Data:** src/cell_table.cpp lines 146-155 (estimate_M_cell function). The bit-packing path (K<=8) computes exact M_cell. For K>8 it falls back to n.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

* **Format:** C++ source.

| Type | Guard |

| **Logic** | Use int64_t for the product to avoid overflow (K=20, 100 cats each = 100^20 overflows int) |
| **Logic** | If product overflows int64_t or exceeds n, return n (safe upper bound) |

title: Epic: Chebyshev, Sinkhorn, Greg Correctness
description:
# Epic: Chebyshev, Sinkhorn, Greg Correctness

## Goal
Fix seven correctness bugs across the three newer solvers (chebyshev IPM, sinkhorn Dykstra, greg Newton QP) that produce wrong results on edge cases or under numerical stress.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] chebyshev: guard convergence check AFTER W<=1e-300 infeasibility check
- [ ] sinkhorn: Dykstra a[] zeroed when !needs_projection (no phantom mass)
- [ ] chebyshev: dual explosion guard uses mu_new (not stale mu)
- [ ] chebyshev: alpha_p/alpha_d floor replaced with safe step clamping that preserves interior invariant
- [ ] greg: N factorization cached; only recomputed when active set changes
- [ ] chebyshev: s_up/s_dn negative slack warns and promotes to INFEAS
- [ ] greg: kMaxNewtonIters=50 or parameterised; NOCONV message populated

## Context & Background
chebyshev is a Mehrotra-style IPM. sinkhorn uses Dykstra KL projections with bisection capacity. greg is a Newton QP solver for chi-square calibration. Each has distinct correctness issues: chebyshev evaluates convergence before infeasibility guard; sinkhorn accumulates phantom KL corrections; greg re-factors the same matrix 10 times needlessly.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Each solver is independent — tasks can run in parallel. TDD throughout. Compile after each file change.

# Epic: Status Code Propagation Fixes

## Goal

title: WU-D: raking.cpp + lbfgsb_solver.cpp — mirror ieppa metric+rule dispatch
description:
WU-D: raking.cpp + lbfgsb_solver.cpp — mirror ieppa metric/rule dispatch

PLAN REF: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-25-convergence-redesign-impl.md §WU-D (Steps D0-D9)

Append to tests/testthat/test-convergence-criteria.R:
  test A3: list(pct=0.001) on raking (seed=43 n=2000 K=2 max_weight=10 500 iter) → status=0, l1_weight_change < 0.001
  test "improvement rule fires on raking": list(improvement=0.001) on raking → status=0, convergence_used$rule=="improvement"
Run: should FAIL before implementation.

FILES: src/raking.cpp, src/raking.hpp, src/lbfgsb_solver.cpp, src/lbfgsb_solver.hpp

RAKING.CPP:
Same pattern as ieppa WU-C. raking uses obs-level weights.
1. l1_weight = Σ|w[i]-w_prev[i]| / st.n  (existing w_prev vector already tracks prev weights)
2. grake_norm: same cells_by_margin_cat-style loop OR use margin accumulation already in raking errRp loop (reuse per-margin S_kj sums)
3. prev_metric_for_rule declared before main loop (no homotopy in raking)
4. Same dispatch switch as ieppa WU-C
5. At exit: res.convergence_metric/rule/tol/iter populated

UPDATE raking.hpp (RakingResult): grake_norm field already added in WU-B, but verify it's initialized to 0.0 in raking.cpp.

LBFGSB_SOLVER.CPP:
lbfgsb is a BATCH solver — single pass. Convergence measured start→final.

1. Save pre-solve weights and compute pre-metrics BEFORE the solve:
   std::vector<double> pre_weights(st.weights, st.weights + st.n);
   LBFGSResult pre_res = compute_final_weights_and_error(st, fn, bounds);
   // compute pre_metric (same type as active metric):
   double pre_metric = 0.0;
   switch (cfg.metric) {
     case lbw::CalibMetric::MAX_ERR:    pre_metric = pre_res.max_error;  break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::MEAN_ERR:   pre_metric = pre_res.mean_error; break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::KL:         pre_metric = pre_res.kl;         break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::CHI2:       pre_metric = pre_res.chi2;       break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::GRAKE_NORM: pre_metric = pre_res.grake_norm; break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::L1_WEIGHT:  pre_metric = 0.0; break; // starts at 0
   }
   // Restore weights (compute_final modifies them):
   std::copy(pre_weights.begin(), pre_weights.end(), st.weights);

2. Actual solve (existing code)

3. After solve: compute final metrics (compute_final_weights_and_error again for finals)
   Also compute l1_weight_change = Σ|w_final[i] - pre_weights[i]| / st.n

4. Convergence dispatch (same switch as ieppa but using pre_metric as "previous"):
   double curr_metric = ...(from final result)...
   IMPROVEMENT: rel = |curr - pre_metric| / pre_metric; converged = rel < pct_tol
   PLATEAU: converged = !(curr < pre_metric * (1 - pct_tol))
   THRESHOLD: converged = curr < pct_tol

5. res.convergence_metric/rule/tol/iter populated

title: WU-4 iEPPA split structural vs transient infeasibility detection
description:
Post-WU-1/2/3 stepstone probe (persistence disabled, 500 iter) showed iEPPA converges to errRp=2.236e-3 on stepstone — better than raking (8.25e-3) and lbfgsb (4.26e-3). However some bucket stays below log_S_kj threshold for 250+ consec iters due to slow co-margin settling (not genuine infeasibility).

Original WU-1 latched persistent_infeas_pairs from both cells.empty() AND log_S_kj<threshold. Split needed:
- cells.empty() + target>0: STATIC condition. Bucket topology fixed. Latch structural_infeas_pairs once (pre-loop scan).
- log_S_kj<threshold: TRANSIENT. Can recover. Used only for infeas_streak (drives WU-3 damping).

Exit status:
- Pre-split: persistent_infeas_pairs non-empty → RK_ERR_INFEAS (fires on stepstone false-positive)
- Post-split: structural_infeas_pairs non-empty → RK_ERR_INFEAS (fires only on genuine no-observations-for-target)
design: Pre-loop scan populates structural_infeas_pairs from cells.empty() AND target>0. infeas_streak[] still tracks transient empties for damping. Fallback blocks do NOT clear structural_infeas_pairs (topology static). Exit sites replaced: persistent_infeas_pairs → structural_infeas_pairs.
acceptance_criteria: Stepstone 3-algo bench: ieppa status RK_OK or NOCONV (NOT INFEAS); errRp <= raking errRp; 181 tests green. WU-1's test-ieppa-persistent-infeas.R test 2 (genuine infeas via zero-obs target) still throws 'persistent empty cell'.
close_reason: WU-4 split landed (1b29df1). Stepstone merge-gate MET: ieppa 3.5s errRp=2.21e-3 (4x better than raking), no INFEAS. 181 tests green. kk1204 per-iter 2.17x unchanged.

title: ieppa: investigate empty-bucket sensitivity — INFEAS on real data
description: Faithful iEPPA at K=9, 836 cats, n=1.58M stepstone data returns RK_ERR_INFEAS at every tested max_weight (5, 10, 50) despite data containing all target categories. Root cause: src/ieppa.cpp triggers is_infeasible when log_S_kj < log(1e-15 * W_input) during Sinkhorn iteration — transient near-zero cells under K=9 overlapping margins flag as infeasible even on feasible inputs. Evidence: stepstone 2026-04-23 bench showed ieppa FAIL, raking 2.3s success, lbfgsb 244s success. Design spec UC-3 favorable regime (M_cell/n=0.0183, 54x compression) WASTED due to solver fragility. Fix options: (a) loosen threshold, (b) distinguish transient vs structural empty, (c) add fallback to skip infeas update without latching flag. Prioritize: high impact (unlocks 54x compression workload class).

title: T13: Phase 2 gate — REFRAME: 30s/<1e-6 unachievable on kk1204 (K=20 dense)
description: Investigation 2026-04-23 (commit 3effd3a, docs/investigations/2026-04-23-kk1204-convergence.md): M_cell/n=1.0 at K=20/uniform random = zero iEPPA compression benefit. Per-iter: ieppa 0.718s, raking 0.033s (22x). ieppa rate ~iter^{-0.5}, extrapolated to 1e-6 ≈ 1.76M iters (~14 days). Gate '<30s AND <1e-6' is structurally unachievable on this input class. REFRAME OPTIONS: (1) accept raking+SQUAREM as the fast path (now achieves stepstone 1.46e-3, 1.6s — 19x faster than autumn), (2) define Phase 2 gate on stepstone instead of kk1204, (3) separately track kk1204 as algorithmic research (leafblower-ylsy).
notes:
2026-04-23 investigation at docs/investigations/2026-04-23-kk1204-convergence.md (commit 3effd3a):
- M_cell/n = 1.0000 at K=20/cat=5/uniform random (zero iEPPA compression benefit)
- Per-iter: ieppa 0.718s, raking 0.033s (22x ratio); lbfgsb 0.352s (11x)
- ieppa sublinear rate ~iter^{-0.5}; extrapolated iter budget to 1e-6 ≈ 1.76M iters (~14 days)
- raking plateaus at 2.2e-2 (near-infeasible at max_weight=3 with skewed targets)
- lbfgsb no demonstrated rate advantage
Conclusion: gate '<30s AND <1e-6' unachievable on this input class with any implemented algorithm. Recommend REFRAME. Follow-ups: leafblower-t2v (doc reframe), leafblower-3c2 (AUTO M_cell/n>0.9 guard), leafblower-2jw (3x3 BLSE sweep).

title: investigate(ieppa+sraa): 20-iter early KL convergence due to SOR disabled
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Understand and document why ieppa+sraa converges in 20 F-evals vs 50 for plain ieppa, and decide whether to fix or accept.
* **Why:** Benchmark shows ieppa+sraa: 20 iters, max_err=1.36e-2 vs plain 50 iters, max_err=2.23e-3. SRAA converges FASTER in KL but at a WORSE max_err point.
* **Root cause (confirmed):** SOR is disabled when accelerate=TRUE (sor_auto_v = sor_cfg.auto_adapt && !st.accelerate). Without SOR damping, BCD sweeps are more aggressive (full omega=1.0 steps). This makes KL converge faster (fewer iters to IMPROVEMENT plateau) but potentially to a different, less max_err-optimal point.
* **Not a convergence check bug:** The CellMetrics.kl eps-smoothing (1e-10) difference from inline marg_kl is negligible. The real cause is SOR=disabled.

## II. Options
A. **Accept**: document that accelerate=TRUE disables SOR and converges faster in KL but may have worse max_err. No code change.
B. **Re-enable SOR for SRAA**: when SRAA steps are rejected (aa=0), SOR should still adapt. Only disable SOR when AA steps ARE accepted (to avoid interference). This requires tracking which steps were AA vs plain.
C. **Add max_err secondary gate**: SRAA convergence also requires max_err < some threshold (e.g. 2x pct_tol) in addition to KL improvement plateau.
D. **Looser IMPROVEMENT tolerance for SRAA**: use pct_tol*10 for the SRAA convergence check to prevent early stop.

## III. Recommendation
Option A (accept for now) + ticket for option B/C in follow-on. The SOR-disabled choice was intentional (competing accelerators). The tradeoff (faster KL, worse max_err) is expected and matches user's statement 'minimizing marginal KL can lead to larger max_err'.

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Verify by running ieppa accelerate=TRUE with explicit sor=NULL vs sor=list(auto=TRUE) — if SOR-re-enabled gives better max_err, option B is worth pursuing
2. Document finding in buglog.json
3. If option B: in SRAA while-loop, detect when SRAA step was plain (r.aa_accepted=false) and allow SOR adaptation on plain steps

## V. Output Schema
```json
{"task_id": "LBW-XXX", "success": true, "data": {"decision": "A|B|C|D", "rationale": "..."}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Root cause verified (SOR disabled → faster KL convergence)
- [ ] Decision documented
- [ ] If fix chosen: implemented and benchmarked
close_reason: Option B implemented: SOR re-enabled on plain SRAA steps. max_err 1.38x (was 6x), aa_count=73 (was 0). Commit 306c5b2.

title: research: SQUAREM overshoots bounded optimum — improve CBB for capacity-constrained calibration
description:
Root cause + fix investigation for SQUAREM quality regression on bounded problems.

## Problem
Stepstone benchmark: raking plain=1.60e-3, raking+squarem=1.75e-3; greenkhorn plain=1.57e-3, greenkhorn+squarem=2.12e-3. SQUAREM consistently overshoots bounded optimum. Autumn SQUAREM achieves 1.60e-3 — proves bounded SQUAREM can work.

## Root cause hypotheses (priority order)
H1: Halving slack too loose (1% allows per-step degradation)
H2: CBB alpha too aggressive; bounded geometry shrinks feasible step
H3: Extrapolation ignores bounds — X_star clamped AFTER extrapolation, not before; correction cannot fully recover
H4: F_eval residual geometry differs: autumn water-fill implicitly constrains step direction
H5: Stale snapshot after fell_back (verify greenkhorn handles this)

## Investigation steps
1. Baseline: verbose=2 on raking+squarem stepstone — count super-steps, fallbacks, bound violations at X_star
2. H1 test: tighten halving from err_star <= err_w2*1.01 to err_star < err_w2*1.001
3. H3 test (projected SQUAREM): clamp X_star to [L,U] BEFORE stabilization F_eval, then rebuild S+W
4. Autumn comparison: run autumn accelerate=FALSE vs TRUE to isolate SQUAREM contribution
5. mSQUAREM: strict monotone (no slack at all) — expected: slower but no overshoot

## DoD
- Root cause confirmed
- Fix in raking.cpp AND greenkhorn.cpp
- Benchmark: raking+squarem <= 1.60e-3, greenkhorn+squarem <= 1.57e-3
- Unbounded tests (T3, T_acc) still GREEN
- devtools::test() FAIL unchanged
notes: 2026-04-29 FINAL: Combined fix implemented (leafblower-zne2). Adaptive sort in f_eval_sraa + outer revert (kSRAAOuterSlack=0.10, kSRAAOuterStallWindow=5). T_sraa_outer_revert GREEN (K=6 basin escape fixed). T_sraa_adaptive_K9/raking_K9 skip in CI (parquet absent). FAIL=3 PASS=493. Commits: greenkhorn.cpp + sraa.hpp (ab0fa02), raking.cpp (81edfe8).
close_reason: DONE: adaptive sort + outer revert fully fixes K=9 stepstone. grk+SRAA 2.12e-3→1.57e-3, rk+SRAA 2.94e-3→1.46e-3. Commits ab0fa02, 81edfe8.

title: S6: Enable _ZGVdN4v_log for lbfgsb Wolfe logit std::log loop
description:

* **Why:** lbfgsb_solver.cpp Wolfe zoom has #pragma omp simd on a loop containing std::log. GCC cannot vectorize std::log to _ZGVdN4v_log without an explicit declaration — the loop scalarizes silently. With the S0 declaration in scope (via lbw_math.hpp include), GCC can auto-vectorize. This ticket verifies and confirms the vectorization.
* **Reference Data:** lbfgsb_solver.cpp Wolfe zoom lines (~lines 402, 527). #pragma omp simd directive. std::log(denom/UmL) inside the loop. After S0: _ZGVdN4v_log is declared in lbw_math.hpp; GCC should auto-vectorize.

title: S4: Vectorize sinkhorn bisect_capacity exp via exp(a[c])*exp(mu) pattern
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Precompute exp_a[c] = exp(a[c]) once before bisection in sinkhorn.cpp; inside the bisection loop compute exp(a[c]+mu) = exp_a[c]*exp(mu) with one scalar exp(mu) per bisection step.
* **Why:** sinkhorn.cpp bisect_capacity inner loop: std::exp(a[c] + mu) per cell, per bisection step. 80 bisection steps × M_cell scalar exps = 80*M_cell calls. Vectorized: compute exp_a[c] once (M_cell _ZGVdN4v_exp calls); per bisection step: compute exp_mu = exp(mu) (1 scalar call); multiply exp_a[c]*exp_mu in vectorized multiply loop. Reduces from 80*M_cell to M_cell vectorized exp calls + 80 scalar.
* **Reference Data:** sinkhorn.cpp bisect_capacity function (lines ~25-40). a[] is a vector of per-cell corrections (constant during one bisection call). mu is the bisection variable (changes each step).

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/sinkhorn.cpp, src/lbw_math.hpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Before bisection loop: compute exp_a[c] = exp(a[c]) for all c using bulk_scaled_exp(1.0, a, exp_a, M_cell) |
| **Logic** | Inside bisection: compute exp_mu = std::exp(mu); then sum += exp_a[c]*exp_mu (vectorized multiply) |
| **Logic** | a[] range: clamped to ±kAmax (typically 700). No overflow risk |
| **Boundary** | exp_a[] pre-allocation: add to scratch buffers declared before the main solver loop |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read sinkhorn.cpp bisect_capacity function — understand a[] and mu.
2. Add exp_a pre-allocation before the solver while-loop.
3. Before each bisect_capacity call: bulk_scaled_exp(1.0, a, exp_a, M_cell).
4. Inside bisection: use exp_a[c]*std::exp(mu) instead of std::exp(a[c]+mu).
5. Benchmark vs baseline.
6. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
7. devtools::test() — sinkhorn tests pass; bisection results identical.
8. Commit: perf(sinkhorn): vectorize bisect_capacity exp via precomputed exp(a[c]) * exp(mu) pattern.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "S4", "success": true, "data": {"exp_calls_reduced": "80*M_cell -> M_cell + 80"}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] exp_a[] precomputed before bisection via bulk_scaled_exp
- [ ] Bisection uses exp_a[c]*exp(mu) pattern
- [ ] Results numerically identical to scalar
- [ ] devtools::test() no regressions; R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds
- [ ] Committed

title: Epic: SIMD Performance — libmvec vectorization
description:
# Epic: SIMD Performance — libmvec vectorization

## Goal
Vectorize all hot scalar log/exp loops over M_cell using glibc libmvec (_ZGVdN4v_log, _ZGVdN4v_exp) for 3-4x speedup in the math-dominated solver paths.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] lbw_math.hpp: _ZGVdN4v_log declared + bulk_log(in, out, n) added (mirrors bulk_scaled_exp)
- [ ] raking.cpp: compute_weight_kl uses bulk_log (3.5x speedup on KL-dominated cases)
- [ ] ieppa.cpp: log(W[c]) in log-path margin sweep precomputed via _ZGVdN4v_log
- [ ] ieppa.cpp: X_tilde rebuild exp(s_clip) uses bulk_exp_clipped via _ZGVdN4v_exp
- [ ] sinkhorn.cpp: bisect_capacity exp vectorized (exp(a[c])*exp(mu) pattern)
- [ ] ieppa.cpp: f_lin correction uses bulk_scaled_exp
- [ ] lbfgsb_solver.cpp: Wolfe logit std::log vectorized via _ZGVdN4v_log declaration
- [ ] All LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC guards in place; non-AVX2 scalar fallback verified

## Context & Background
Current lbw_math.hpp has bulk_scaled_exp (using _ZGVdN4v_exp) for exp only. Six hot loops use scalar std::log or std::exp over M_cell cells (up to 2M on stepstone). Adding _ZGVdN4v_log declaration and bulk_log helper unblocks the majority. Sinkhorn bisection does 80 steps x M_cell scalar exp calls -- vectorizable as exp(a[c])*exp(mu).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
S0 (lbw_math.hpp _ZGVdN4v_log + bulk_log) MUST land before S1-S6. S1-S5 can then run in parallel (different files). Benchmark before/after each change with bench::mark().

title: WU-2 iEPPA linear-space Sinkhorn dispatch at M_cell/n > 0.5
description:
Runtime dispatch in src/ieppa.cpp: log-space path retained when M_cell/n < 0.5; switch to linear-space multiplicative updates when M_cell/n >= 0.5 (kLinearSpaceThreshold=2.0 compression cutoff). Overflow trip = pow(DBL_MAX/(2*max_X_init), 1/K). On trip: full state reset + restart in log-space (one-shot, linear_fallback_used guard).

Env var LBW_IEPPA_FORCE_PATH={linear,log,unset} for tests (always compiled, microsecond getenv cost). Closes kk1204 per-iter gap (22x raking) at dense compression. Depends on WU-1 lambdas (record_empty/record_nonempty).

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-23-ieppa-convergence-hardening-impl.md Task 2 (Steps 2.1-2.12).
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-23-ieppa-convergence-hardening-design.md WU-2.

title: raking descent monitor: window_min never updates from +inf sentinel
description: Observed in docs/investigations/2026-04-23-kk1204-convergence.md (commit 3effd3a). Stall message reports 'window_min=inf' — the monitor never updated min_errRp_window from its +inf initial value. Root cause (reading src/raking.cpp P1.2.1 code): at iter 1, rel_eps = 0.01 * inf = inf, eps = max(inf, tol_abs) = inf, so the improvement branch's comparison 'errRp < min_errRp_window - eps' becomes 'errRp < -inf' which fails; n_no_improve increments from iter 1 regardless of trajectory. Fix: initialize min_errRp_window from iter 1's observed errRp, OR short-circuit the eps computation when min_errRp_window is infinite. Does not affect abort behaviour on observed inputs (iters 20-40 are genuinely stalled) but misleads operators via the diagnostic text.

title: research: greenkhorn vs autumn quality difference — algorithm and parameter analysis
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Understand and document why greenkhorn (1.57e-3) differs from autumn (1.60e-3) on stepstone.
* **Why:** Greenkhorn should be analogous to autumn's greedy rake. The difference could indicate: (1) different convergence criteria, (2) different algorithm (single-margin vs all-K rounds), (3) autumn benchmark params mismatch, or (4) SQUAREM in autumn overshoots the bounded optimum.
* **Reference Data:** Cached autumn result: 33.6s, max_err=1.5996e-3 (from stepstone_reference_autumn_only.rds). Autumn was run with accelerate=TRUE (SQUAREM+greedy). Greenkhorn benchmark: 3.3s, max_err=1.5714e-3 (single-margin steps per iteration, no SQUAREM actually active due to harvest.R bug leafblower-e0zb). Both use max_weight=5, min_weight=0.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** benchmarks/stepstone_all_methods.R, tests/testthat/fixtures/stepstone_reference_autumn_only.rds, autumn source.
* **Format:** R analysis.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Report max_err, L1, marg_kl, DEFF, ESS for both methods |
| **Logic** | Report autumn cached params (max_weight, convergence criterion, accelerate setting) |
| **Logic** | After leafblower-e0zb fix: re-run greenkhorn+squarem and compare to greenkhorn+plain |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read stepstone_reference_autumn_only.rds — what params was it captured with?
2. Compare greenkhorn (plain, no SQUAREM) vs autumn (SQUAREM+greedy rounds): are they the same algorithm?
3. After e0zb fix: run greenkhorn+squarem; compare to autumn+SQUAREM quality.
4. Document the algorithm differences in a beads memory entry.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "grk_autumn_analysis", "success": true, "data": {"algorithm_difference": "...", "quality_comparison": "..."}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Root cause of 1.57 vs 1.60 documented
- [ ] Greedy-single-step vs greedy-all-K-rounds difference explained
- [ ] After e0zb fix: does greenkhorn+squarem match autumn quality?
close_reason:
Answered by benchmark results after e0zb fix:
- greenkhorn plain (1.57e-3) vs autumn (1.60e-3): different algorithms (single-margin steps vs K-step greedy rounds), different fixed points — expected.
- greenkhorn+squarem (2.12e-3): SQUAREM overshoots bounded optimum, tracked in leafblower-i0am.
- Correlation with ieppa: r=0.980 (plain), r=0.958 (squarem). Both acceptable.
Core question resolved. Documentation value minimal — closing.

title: decision: expose alm_mu to R or drop ALM penalty path from ieppa_soft
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Decide whether to expose alm_mu as a harvest() parameter or remove the dead ALM penalty code from ieppa.cpp.
* **Why:** alm_mu is hardcoded to 0 in r_bridge.cpp:316 and never reachable from R. The ADMM z-update (use_admm_capacity) runs independently and works fine. The ALM penalty path (lines 386-387 in ieppa.cpp) is unreachable.
* **Reference Data:** src/r_bridge.cpp:316-317 (alm_lambda=0, alm_mu=0 hardcoded). src/ieppa.cpp:355 (alm_mu_base), 386-387 (dead ALM scaling). src/types.hpp: alm_lambda/alm_mu fields on CalibState.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Source review of ieppa.cpp ALM path + decision from user.
* **Format:** Design decision.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Option A: expose alm_mu as harvest() param — adds API surface, enables ALM penalty scaling along homotopy levels |
| **Logic** | Option B: remove alm_mu/alm_lambda from CalibState + ieppa.cpp — cleans dead code, simplifies API |
| **Logic** | ieppa_soft ADMM z-update (u[c]) works correctly with alm_mu=0 — not a correctness issue |
| **Boundary** | ABI change if alm_mu/alm_lambda removed from CalibState (rk_result_t unchanged) |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. User decides: expose or remove.
2. If expose: add alm_mu param to harvest.R, wire in r_bridge.cpp, document in harvest.Rd.
3. If remove: delete alm_mu/alm_lambda from CalibState, remove dead ALM path in ieppa.cpp.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "alm_mu_decision", "success": true, "data": {"decision": "expose|remove"}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Decision made and implemented
- [ ] If expose: alm_mu in harvest.R docs + r_bridge wired
- [ ] If remove: no dead ALM code remains in ieppa.cpp
notes: DECISION RESOLVED: expose alm_mu as harvest() parameter. The user intended ALM (Augmented Lagrangian Method) to replace the hard capacity cap in ieppa_soft. alm_lambda/alm_mu fields in CalibState were designed for this but never wired to the capacity BCD block. Implementation needed: (1) expose alm_mu in harvest.R; (2) wire per-cell ALM dual update in ieppa.cpp capacity block (replace or gate the hard clamp); (3) the existing u[] ADMM vector is the correct per-cell storage for ALM duals. Spec doc incorrectly called this ADMM — it should be ALM.
close_reason: Decision: Option A — expose alm_mu to R. Implementation: add harvest() parameter 'alm_penalty' that sets st.alm.mu. capacity_penalty already covers capacity_mu (separate). Small bridge + docstring change needed.

title: S5: Use bulk_scaled_exp for f_lin correction in ieppa.cpp T1.B block

* **Reference Data:** ieppa.cpp line 670 (T1.B correction block). total_cats = sum(cat_counts[k]) + K. f_lin[j] = std::exp(lf[cat_offset[k]+j]) in a loop.

| **Logic** | Verify lf and f_lin are contiguous vectors of the right size |
| **Boundary** | total_cats is small; speedup is minimal. This is a hygiene fix. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

3. Replace the loop with bulk_scaled_exp.
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.

**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Remove always-true !W_best.empty() from sinkhorn.cpp:204; document apply_rule prev-update side effect in calib_dispatch.hpp:99.
* **Why:** S4: W_best declared as vector(ct.M_cell,0.0) — never empty. Dead condition creates false impression of empty path. S5: apply_rule always updates prev regardless of return value (sliding-window baseline); undocumented surprises future readers.
* **Reference Data:** sinkhorn.cpp:204 — if (std::isfinite(best_metric_seen) && !W_best.empty()). calib_dispatch.hpp:99 — prev = curr; // always update.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Current source files (independent of all other tasks).
* **Format:** C++17 source edits (2 files). Requires recompile for sinkhorn change.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **S4** | Remove && !W_best.empty() only. Keep std::isfinite(best_metric_seen) check. |
| **S5** | Add comment only — do not change logic. |
| **Compile** | R CMD INSTALL --preclean required (sinkhorn.cpp change). |
| **No behavior change** | Both edits are documentation/dead-code only. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. sinkhorn.cpp:204 — remove && !W_best.empty() from the if condition.
2. calib_dispatch.hpp:99 — add comment: // always update — sliding-window baseline for next call.
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean.
4. devtools::test() FAIL ≤ 3.
5. Commit.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
Both files committed. Build DONE.

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] !W_best.empty() removed from sinkhorn.cpp:204
- [ ] Comment added to calib_dispatch.hpp:99
- [ ] Build succeeds
- [ ] devtools::test() FAIL ≤ 3
- [ ] Commit message starts 'simplify:'

The &&!W_best.empty() condition adds zero safety, creates false impression there's an empty path. S5: apply_rule always updates prev (sliding-window baseline for next call) regardless of return value — this is intentional but surprising to readers. Comment prevents future devs from 'optimizing' it away.

title: kk1204 convergence research: algorithmic replacement for slow-rate regime
description: Empirical finding (2026-04-24): kk1204 (n=1M, K=20, max_weight=3) exhibits PURE SLOW-RATE Sinkhorn convergence. errRp trajectory strictly monotone-decreasing, rate ≈ iter^{-0.5} asymptotic. No oscillation. Fixed-point accelerators explored and rejected: APVA (P2.2c), Joint Anderson (P2.2b), Halpern mixing (P2.2d). UPDATE 2026-04-28: raking+SQUAREM with geometry fix (obs-level CBB norms) achieves stepstone fulldata 1.46e-3 max_err in 1.6s (19x faster than autumn 30.8s). However kk1204 is a fundamentally different problem — K=20 dense with M_cell/n=1.0 gives zero iEPPA compression; ieppa 22x slower than raking per-iter. kk1204 slow-rate is still unresolved for iEPPA-class solvers. Open research: Newton on constraint duals, Chambolle-Pock primal-dual, or mirror descent with entropic regularization (per memory fixed-point-accelerators-apva-anderson-joint-anderson-on).
acceptance_criteria: Decision: either ship P2.1-state as kk1204's practical answer OR commit to one algorithmic replacement pathway. Not an implementation ticket — research first.

title: WU-3 iEPPA adaptive damping auto-triggered on persistence stress
description:
Geometric-blend damping in src/ieppa.cpp: lf_new = alpha*(log_target - log_S_kj) + (1-alpha)*lf_old. Default alpha=1.0 via explicit if-branch (std::pow(_, 1.0) is NOT a no-op — full transcendental cost). Auto-engages alpha=0.5 when infeas_streak[idx] >= kInfeasPersistence/2; latched per-solve.

Env var LBW_IEPPA_FORCE_DAMPING={on,off,unset} for tests (mandatory for falsifiable iter_damped > iter_stable assertion per spec §7 / CTO B5). Step 3.6.5 patches WU-2 fallback blocks to also reset alpha/damped_latched (spec §5 state-clean checklist).

Tang 2024 (arxiv:2403.05054) Theorem 1 K-counting: K indexes INEQUALITY constraints, NOT problem dimensions. For iEPPA box-constraints L ≤ X[c] ≤ U, K_ineq = 2·M_cell (two per cell: upper and lower bounds), not K=20 margin count. Misreading inflates error bound 8·n^(2/(K+1))·(K+1)·exp(-η·Δ/(K+1)) to vacuously large — at 2·M_cell=2e6, exp(-47·Δ) becomes exp(-2.4e-5·Δ·η). Paper's K=O(1) assumption doesn't transfer to box-constraint case.

Cell-level norms vs obs-level norms: in leafblower cell-table code, Σ_c r_c² ≠ Σ_i r_i² when n_per_cell[c] varies. Equivalence requires 1/n_c weighting: Σ_c r_c²/n_c = Σ_i r_i². Any algorithm needing obs-level L2 geometry (CBB, SQUAREM) MUST use inv_nc = 1.0/n_per_cell[c]. Raw cell-level sums over-weight large cells.

errRp oscillates near constrained KL minimum, weight KL is monotone: errRp stall fires prematurely (stepstone: 2.98e-3 with errRp stall vs 1.60e-3 with KL stall). Use KL stall for flat raking loop. Sinkhorn-style K-way multiplicative sweeps: naive O(K^2·M_cell) per iter (K-1 multiplications per cell per margin) collapses to O(K·M_cell) via prefactored per-cell accumulator X_cur[c] = X_init[c]·W[c]·∏_m f[m][g_m(c)]. Per-bucket: divide out f_kj_old once per cell to get margin-k-removed sum; after update, rescale X_cur for bucket cells by f_new/f_old. Measured 22x→1.96x ratio vs raking on kk1204 K=20 dense regime.

SQUAREM extrapolation anti-pattern: 'auto X_star = X_snap; for (c) X_star[c] = X_snap[c] - expr;' — the initial copy is 100% wasted bandwidth because every element is immediately overwritten by the fill loop. Remove the copy; only the fill loop is needed. For stepstone M_cell≈2M, initial + up to kMaxHalvings=16 copies = up to 17×16MB = 272MB wasted bandwidth per super-step. Fixed in 7f17e8f.

SQUAREM CBB step requires obs-level weighted norms: alpha = -norm(r)/norm(v) must use Σ r_c²/n_c (NOT Σ r_c²). Cell-level norms over-weight large cells (n_c=hundreds), causing over-extrapolation → step-halving collapses α≈-1 → no acceleration. Fix: multiply by 1.0/ct.n_per_cell[c] in norm accumulation. Also keep separate v_sq_cell (without 1/n_c) for halving criterion — both sides of halving must be in same geometry (cell-level). Verified stepstone: cell-level gave 1.71e-3, obs-level gave 1.46e-3 (beats autumn 1.60e-3).

Greenkhorn (Altschuler-Weed-Rigollet 2017, arxiv:1705.09634, NIPS) = iEPPA-preserving backing for P-B priority-ordered margin scheduler. One greedy-argmax coordinate per iteration (pick row/column with max marginal residual) achieves near-linear time on binary Sinkhorn with same theoretical guarantees as alternating. Multi-marginal K-way + box-constraint extension is design-transparent (priority queue keyed on errRp_k) but not proved in surveyed literature; transfer conjectural. Empirically closes autumn's greedy-rake-polishes-simple-margins advantage within iEPPA semantics.

Cell-order scatter within margin k is bit-identical to per-bucket loop because cells partition disjointly by category. Plan's naive K-loop rebuilds were wasteful; subagent's shortcuts verified correct.

After SQUAREM accepts a step, calling compute_cell_metrics(st, ct, X, W, bucket) is a second O(K×M_cell) pass — same bucket aggregation just done inside F_eval via compute_errRp_ct. Fix: replace compute_errRp_ct in F_eval with compute_cell_metrics storing into last_F_metrics (captured by lambda), then reuse last_F_metrics in convergence block. W_total inside F_eval post-hyperplane = st.n exactly.

ieppa.cpp BUDGET/STALL reclassification block (inserted after homotopy loop end) MUST come AFTER the INFEAS promotion guard that checks res.status == RK_ERR_NOCONV. If inserted before: infeasible problems exit with BUDGET(4) instead of INFEAS(2), harvest() warns instead of stop(). Fix: extend INFEAS guard to also match BUDGET and STALL. Discovered 2026-04-28 during C2 fix implementation.

r_bridge.cpp auto-dispatch fallback: BUDGET(4) should trigger fallback to lbfgsb (same semantics as old NOCONV — still improving, just ran out of time). STALL(5) should NOT trigger fallback (at constrained optimum, lbfgsb won't help). Condition: 'res_status == RK_ERR_NOCONV || res_status == RK_ERR_BUDGET'. Also: INFEAS promotion check in ieppa.cpp must cover BUDGET/STALL or infeasible problems bypass stop() in harvest.R.

F_eval must be stateless for SQUAREM L2 halving: with Dykstra p[]/q_hyp correction vectors accumulated across F calls, norm(F(X*)-X*) is inflated by correction effects that explode on zeroed cells. Water-filling (stateless F) makes L2 criterion geometrically correct. Root cause of L2 halving failures before Dykstra→water-filling refactor.

Greedy scheduler inside SQUAREM degrades CBB: Greedy re-sorts margins by errRp_k before each F call making F non-stationary. SQUAREM requires identical F for both F(X) and F(F(X)). Solution: force round_robin when accelerate=TRUE. In harvest.R: 'if (accelerate_bool && scheduler==greedy) scheduler <- round_robin'.

RK_ERR_BUDGET=4 vs RK_ERR_STALL=5 in leafblower.h: status=1 (NOCONV) conflated budget exhausted (prescription: increase max_iterations) vs loss plateau (prescription: accept result). New codes: BUDGET=4 (loss still decreasing), STALL=5 (at constrained optimum). harvest.R: budget → warning to increase budget; stall → 'weights valid, no further improvement achievable'.

Fixed-point accelerators (APVA Anderson, joint Anderson on lf+logW, Halpern mixing) ALL fail on capacity-clamp non-smooth operators in slow-rate regimes like kk1204 (K=20, n=1M, max_weight=3). Root cause: piecewise-linearity defeats contraction theory; slow-rate ≠ oscillation. Requires algorithmic replacement class (Newton on constraint duals, Chambolle-Pock primal-dual, mirror descent with entropic regularization), not acceleration overlay.

logit Newton (logit_calib.cpp) fails silently on K>=6 problems with overlapping/redundant margin constraints because AA^T*D is rank-deficient — fixed via adaptive LDLT eps=max(1e-10, max_b/kMaxDeltaZ) and init sanity check (max_lambda<=10), but convergence quality degrades on highly collinear constraints. Alternative: raking or ieppa for such problems. Commit d0757d7 (2026-04-29).

Schmitzer 2019 (arxiv:1610.06519, SIAM SISC) epsilon-scaling + log-domain stabilization + Chizat 2024 (arxiv:2408.11620) annealed-Sinkhorn theorem (beta_t=Theta(sqrt(t)) universal schedule, necessary beta_t->inf AND beta_t-beta_{t-1}->0) jointly provide the theoretical backing for iEPPA-preserving progressive bound tightening (P-A). max_weight plays an epsilon-like role: loose = smooth/fast, tight = piecewise-linear/slow. Annealing max_weight from target*k down to target across outer iEPPA sweeps is the direct structural analog. Rate transfer from 1D Sinkhorn to K-way box-constrained iEPPA is by analogy, empirically validated not proved.
